To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the governance mechanisms within Wikipedia appear to be effective in achieving social self regulation.
Wikipedians appear to use linguistic cues to coordinate their behaviour in ways which are consistent with the predictions of normative theory.
Wikipedians appear to use normative mechanisms in a sophisticated way to achieve social self-regulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how social self-regulation can be achieved in the absence of centralised governance.
the question of how norms are created and enforced in a community which is distributed across the Internet.
the governance mechanisms within a distributed on-line community, Wikipedia, and in particular with the role of norm-based mechanisms in achieving social order.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
normative mechanisms are important for social self-regulation within Wikipedia and that they are likely to be important within other on-line communities.
Wikipedia is a community that has a strong sense of self-regulating norms and values.
the Wikipedia is a complex and dynamic social system, which has been able to self-organise into a functioning social order.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Wikipedia appears to be governed by norms and these norms have an important role to play in the achievement of self-regulation.
Wikipedia is an interesting case study in the study of social self-regulation in computer mediated communities.
we have identified the need for a more sophisticated model of normative behaviour than has been used in past attempts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the normative mechanisms which are used to coordinate social self-regulation are not as straightforward as has been assumed in previous research.
the cognitive processes involved in the use of linguistic cues are complex.
there is a need to develop new approaches to modelling the cognitive processes that are used to implement social self-regulation.
